artifacts.summary: Maps the parent plan's Phase 4 (restack-on-merge) design onto the live review-stack-prepare.sh code: reusable primitives, manifest schema, dispatcher/flag gaps, three PD7 ambiguities with recommended readings, exit-code allocation, and reusable test-fixture scaffolding.

memory_candidates.content: In review-stack-prepare.sh, rsp_move_commit_onto_new_parent (three-way git merge-tree with --merge-base, refusing with a named-path conflict) is designed as the one primitive serving both cut's base-move step and any future restack recompute step (PD6's explicit intent). When extending a script built this way, check whether a 'new' operation is actually a second call site for an existing primitive before writing a new wrapper.

Simulating 'the remote already received this' in review-stack-prepare.sh's test suite never uses a real git push or fetch: it writes directly to refs/remotes/<remote>/<ref> via git update-ref (and git commit-tree for synthetic foreign/merge commits), consistent with the script's own no-push/no-fetch static assertions. This is the established technique for any future subcommand's remote-tracking-ref fixtures in this suite.

The git[[:space:]]+merge([[:space:]]|$) static-assertion regex style (used in test-review-stack-prepare.sh to forbid bare 'git merge' without blocking 'git merge-tree'/'git merge-base') is a reusable pattern for any suite that needs to forbid one git subcommand while explicitly permitting its plumbing cousins with the same prefix.
